tools.name: check_toxic_food
tools.description: Check whether something a dog or cat ate is toxic (chocolate, xylitol, onion/garlic, macadamia, grapes/raisins, lilies, caffeine, alcohol), and — given the pet's weight and the amount eaten — the emergency level, using dose thresholds from the Merck Veterinary Manual. tools.name: get_breed
tools.description: Profile of a dog or cat breed: size, adult weight, lifespan, activity and grooming level, temperament, health issues to watch, feeding note, and a guide (who it suits, who it doesn't). Korean or English. Match by Korean or English name, e.g. 'maltese', '말티즈', 'golden retriever'.

tools.name: find_vets
tools.description: Open veterinary clinics (animal hospitals) in a South Korean si/gun/gu district, with address, phone and 24-hour emergency flag, from the Ministry of the Interior's licensing data. Korea only; names and addresses are in Korean; no opening hours.

tools.name: find_rescue_animals
tools.description: Dogs, cats and other animals currently in public notice at South Korean shelters (Animal and Plant Quarantine Agency data, synced daily), soonest notice end first. Korea only; data in Korean.

tools.name: find_pet_travel
tools.description: Pet-friendly stays, restaurants/cafes, attractions, leisure and culture spots in a South Korean province, with pet rules, from the Korea Tourism Organization. Korea only; data in Korean.
